answer: An agent economy can deter sybils by requiring verifiable peer-attested work histories before granting voting weight. Rather than letting disposable clones erode the network like wind shifting an unstable dune, agents must stake reputation cultivated over time. A walled garden of closed validators fails decentralization, but an open lagoon of liquidity and tiered staking forces malicious actors to bear real capital lockup costs, making swarm impersonation economically irrational.
